scope: Only the registered histories/shapes are classified. Existing MariaDB differential, transaction, storage and fault suites remain separate release requirements; this manifest is not a blanket MySQL equivalence claim.

contracts.description: Session and gateway-global isolation/lock timeout are distinct; new connections inherit globals.
READ COMMITTED sees committed changes and its own writes; rollback removes own changes.
Duplicate multi-row INSERT rolls back that statement; savepoint rollback preserves earlier writes.
1205/HY000 rolls back the waiting statement; preceding transaction writes can commit.
A conflicting READ COMMITTED update waits, then updates the newly committed value.
NOWAIT returns 3572/HY000; SKIP LOCKED returns the unlocked row. MariaDB supplemental control uses 1205/HY000.
Successful CREATE TABLE commits preceding writes; later ROLLBACK does not undo them.
Enabling autocommit commits the pending transaction.
Unchanged UPDATE reports zero or one with CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS; changed UPDATE reports one.
Text and COM_STMT parameter binding preserve exact point-read and UPDATE results.
REPEATABLE READ uses strict serializability: stale read validation aborts COMMIT with 1213/40001.
REPEATABLE READ rejects write skew under Tarn strict serializability; InnoDB snapshot isolation permits this history.
Tarn exposes requested session isolation, effective default, pending one-shot setting and active effective isolation.
SET tarn_isolation_contract=MYSQL is refused with 1235/42000; no exact InnoDB isolation mode is advertised.
READ COMMITTED ordinary and current reads see intervening committed inserts/updates.
A REPEATABLE READ predicate invalidated by an insert fails Tarn commit validation; MySQL can commit its snapshot.
An unchanged serializable UPDATE holds no Tarn write lock; InnoDB still locks the matched row.
A two-row deadlock aborts one entire transaction with 1213/40001; the survivor commits exactly one increment per key.
Unsupported GLOBAL autocommit/sql_mode assignments fail with 1235/42000 before changing session behavior or committing buffered writes. Only isolation and lock-timeout have mutable gateway defaults.
INSERT IGNORE preserves accepted rows and reports warning level/code 1062; unknown columns report 1054/42S22. Error message wording is outside this entry.

A 10,000-row indexed READ COMMITTED scan overlapping bounded key movement must return every key once. Tarn may explicitly refuse a read with 1213/40001; InnoDB reads its statement snapshot. At least three complete scans and observed overlap are required.
Two READ COMMITTED shared-lock upgrades choose one 1213/40001 victim; only the survivor increment commits.
Two-row READ COMMITTED and SERIALIZABLE commits preserve exact values; Tarn runtime counters prove the local path.
Two-row READ COMMITTED and SERIALIZABLE commits preserve exact values across shards; Tarn runtime counters prove two-phase commit.

Seventy ignored duplicates leave data unchanged, report warning_count 70 and retain 64 messages (max_error_count=64). SHOW WARNINGS preserves diagnostics. SELECT count, expression SELECT and SET capture prior counts then clear messages/counts; a DML count reference captures the prior count while publishing only its own warnings. Literal/comment diagnostic words do not preserve old warnings.
Tarn supports max_error_count=64/DEFAULT and refuses other limits with 1235/42000 without changing the limit; MySQL supports a configurable limit.
Text SET captures prior warning totals. Tarn binary SET captures each execution's prior total on fresh/reused handles; MySQL rejects the binary form with 1295/HY000 without assigning the variable.

Text warning-count readers and arithmetic agree. Binary bare readers return the prior total on Tarn; MySQL rejects them with 1295/HY000. Binary arithmetic is refused with Tarn 1235/42000 versus MySQL 1295/HY000.
